summary_en: Attached to an adjective, it describes a change of state: getting colder, getting busier, getting better.
ja_diff_note: Same idea as 寒くなる, but Korean fuses 지다 onto the 아/어 form instead of adding a separate なる; for nouns ('become a teacher') Korean uses 되다. On action verbs -아/어지다 turns passive-like (만들어지다 = 作られる), which くなる never does.
notes: Adjective stem + 아/어 + 지다: 춥다 -> 추워지다, 크다 -> 커지다, 바쁘다 -> 바빠지다, 좋다 -> 좋아지다.
Then conjugate 지다 as usual: 추워졌어요 (got cold), 추워질 거예요 (will get cold), 추워지고 있어요 (is getting cold).
Nouns take 되다, not 지다: 선생님이 됐어요.
Don't confuse with -아/어하다 (좋아해요 = likes) or -게 되다 (end up doing, mostly with verbs).

examples.ko: 날씨가 많이 추워졌어요. 텃밭 채소는 괜찮아요?
examples.en: The weather has gotten really cold. Are the garden vegetables okay?
examples.ja: だいぶ寒くなりましたね。畑の野菜は大丈夫ですか。

examples.en: Your Korean has gotten so much better!
examples.ja: 韓国語、ほんとに上手になったね！

drills.prompt_en: Work has gotten really busy lately.
drills.explain_en: 바쁘다 drops ㅡ before 아 (바빠), then adds 지다; 바빠하다 means 'act busy', not 'become busy'.

drills.prompt_en: Now that I've eaten, I feel better.
drills.explain_en: 좋아지다 = to get better (良くなる); 좋아했어 means 'liked'.

drills.prompt_en: 준수 has gotten a lot taller!
drills.explain_en: 크다 drops ㅡ to 커, then adds 지다: 커졌네.

drills.prompt_en: My friend will become a teacher next year.
drills.explain_en: With a noun, 'become' is 이/가 되다; 지다 only attaches to adjectives here.
